discovery.issue: Packing many otherwise independent M2 configurations into one large solve_ivp state vector causes SciPy RK45 to use one shared adaptive error norm and one shared step sequence. The physical equations remain uncoupled, but the numerical pass/fail result can depend on shard composition near discontinuous acceptance events such as the first 90 C crossing.
discovery.interpretation: Vectorized multi-configuration solves are suitable for screening and diagnostics but are not authoritative for per-configuration acceptance classification.

independent_adjudication.reconciled_count_caution: 284 is not represented as a complete independent scalar enumeration of all 4000 configurations. It is the common batch classification plus independent scalar adjudication of every observed batch disagreement.

authoritative_execution_rule.per_configuration_solver: one independent scipy.solve_ivp RK45 integration of the four-state M2 system
authoritative_execution_rule.source_profile_interpolation: unchanged authoritative ValidationDataset linear interpolation semantics
authoritative_execution_rule.parallelism: parallel independent processes are permitted because each process owns a separate four-state RK45 solve and adaptive controller
authoritative_execution_rule.compiled_rhs: A compiled implementation may accelerate RHS arithmetic only if it preserves the frozen equations and is spot-checked against the committed M2SimulationRunner. SciPy solve_ivp remains the integrator and controller.

prior_checkpoint_disposition.reason: The checkpoint used shared-adaptive-controller vectorized ensembles. It remains useful as qualitative accumulating falsification evidence, but its exact counts must not be used for the final M2 gate.
